He said political parties must look beyond winning elections and invest in the knowledge, expertise and structures needed to govern effectively. items.title: Six dead after gunman opens fire in Kraków market square, with three more victims found at suspect’s home
items.summary: Suspect was influenced by far-right ideology and held ‘ultra-nationalistic’ views, says Polish interior minister Six people have been killed and 16 wounded after a gunman opened fire in a busy market square in Kraków, authorities said, in what Poland’s defence minister called an “act of terror” on the people of the city. The suspect, a 25-year-old Polish citizen, opened fire with an automatic weapon in the city’s main square at about 3pm on Saturday. Continue reading...

items.title: Ebola: Why is there still no vaccine?
items.summary: Ebola has been known about for decades, but there is still no vaccine against the Bundibugyo strain of the virus causing the current outbreak. New research raises hopes of protection against the various types of Ebola.

items.title: Armenia's selective prosecution: A threat to EU relations?

items.summary: Near-final results show South Africa's once dominant ANC will see its lowest-ever vote percentage. The party is taking the blame for shoddy municipal services, including water and electricity shortages.

items.title: Son of Iran's shah receives 'Freedom Prize' in Frankfurt
items.summary: 18,000 people gathered in Frankfurt to show support for Reza Pahlavi, the son of the Iranian monarch ousted in 1979. Factions in the opposition have accused him of not distancing himself from his father's rule.

items.title: After victory in the midterms, what next for US Democrats?
items.summary: Donald Trump's Republican party has lost its majority in both chambers of the US Congress. But the president still has a lot of power — and the Democrats have yet to agree on how best to use theirs.

items.title: Tenerife honour teammate Jesus De Miguel with tearful tribute
items.summary: Tenerife’s stadium filled up with thousands of mourners on Saturday where they held a tearful tribute to striker Jesus De Miguel, who passed away after colliding with a goalkeeper during a match, subsequently suffering a cardiac arrest. "To speak of you in the past tense ​is tremendously unfair," team captain Enric Gallego said.

items.title: Gunmen kills six in Krakow, three more bodies found at his house
items.summary: A chilling new discovery in Poland, where three bodies have reportedly been found inside the Krakow gunman's home. That's in addition to six people killed and sixteen wounded when the attacker opened fire in the city's historic square. Prime Minister Donald Tusk has now declared the shooting an act of terrorism, saying Poland has never experienced anything quite like it. The 25-year-old suspect, described by authorities as holding radical far-right views, was shot by police.

items.title: 'A violent fighter and warrior': Trump offers press secretary role to UFC chief Dana White
items.summary: US President Donald Trump on Saturday said he was asking mixed martial arts promoter Dana White to be the new White House press secretary. Trump has repeatedly tried to hitch his MAGA brand of politics to White's enormously successful Ultimate Fighting Championship.

items.title: France Unbowed’s Mélenchon unveils ‘A Shared Future’ manifesto ahead of 2027 presidential race
items.summary: “We are facing a crisis of human civilisation. And we are going to win.” A defiant Jean-Luc Mélenchon was in fighting mood today as he presented his presidential manifesto at Le Bourget, north of Paris. It is his fourth bid for the French presidency, and he has chosen a venue steeped in left-wing campaign history: the site of François Hollande's famous 2012 rally.

items.title: 🔴 Israeli president picks Netanyahu's rival Eisenkot to try to form government
Israeli president picks Netanyahu's rival Eisenkot to try to form government
items.summary: Israeli President Isaac Herzog picked former military chief Gadi Eisenkot to try to form a government, he said in a statement Saturday. Last month's parliamentary elections left neither Eisenkot nor Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu with a clear path to building a majority.

items.title: 'We must change everything': French far-left leader Mélenchon launches presidential programme
items.summary: Veteran leftist Jean-Luc Mélenchon formally announced his plan to raise France's minimum wage, cap prices for essential foods and restore the country's retirement age to 60 in a speech launching his 2027 presidential election programme on Saturday. Polls currently indicate that he is the left wing's strongest contender against far-right candidate Marine Le Pen.

items.title: France investigating if bogus bomb threats against airlines linked to 'foreign powers'
items.summary: French prosecutors are investigating a series of fake bomb threats that targeted commercial flights in Europe this week, including trying to establish whether foreign powers may be involved. Those responsible for the bogus threats have not been identified.

items.title: Poland: Footage shows people taking cover as a gunman opens fire in Krakow
items.summary: Footage shows people fleeing as cars speed away during a deadly shooting at Krakow's Main Market Square, which left six people dead and about 15 injured.

items.title: Ukraine: Russian strikes hit Kyiv region, damaging infrastructure
items.summary: Russian strikes have damaged infrastructure in the Kyiv region and left a kindergarten in ruins in the Ukrainian capital. Firefighters battled a major blaze as Ukraine faced renewed attacks on its energy network.

items.title: Heavy rains leave tens of thousands without shelter in Gaza
items.summary: Tens of thousands of displaced families in the Gaza Strip spent a sleepless night on Saturday, as heavy rain flooded their fragile tents, and soaked their mattresses and belongings.

items.title: Pope Leo begins South America tour in 'fairly good shape' after cancer treatment
items.summary: Pope Leo XIV declared he was in "fairly good shape" after his cancer treatment, as he kicked off a three-nation South America tour on Friday.
